issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaks from CI workaround into core/setup.py runtime install_requires.
issues.detail: All six reviewers flag this as the central issue. The mmcv/pkg_resources build problem is CI-scoped, but pinning setuptools<82 in core/setup.py propagates the cap to every downstream autogluon user forever. Scope the pin to CI scripts (where the FIXMEs already live) or to a build-time extra, not the public runtime contract.

issues.description: Three independent setuptools<82 pins with no shared source of truth or revert criterion.
issues.detail: env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py each independently assert setuptools<82, and only two carry the mmcv#3325 FIXME. There is no stated postcondition for removal and no shared constant, so when upstream fixes the bug the operator must remember all three sites. Add a single revert criterion and link the pins.

issues.description: mmdet silently bumped 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no justification in the diff.
issues.detail: The PR is framed as a setuptools/mmengine CI fix, but mmdet also moves a minor version. No reviewer can tell whether 3.3.0 is required for mmengine 0.10.7 / mmcv 2.1.0 compatibility or is incidental scope creep. Either split the change or add a one-line rationale in the commit body.

issues.description: --no-build-isolation silently couples mmcv build to ambient env state without comment.
issues.detail: Disabling build isolation makes the mmcv build depend on whatever setuptools and torch are present in the active interpreter. This works only because setuptools<82 is pinned two lines earlier, but the ordering invariant is unstated and brittle. A one-line comment explaining why isolation is disabled would let the next maintainer remove it safely.

issues.description: mim-to-pip switch drops dependency-matching logic without documentation.
issues.detail: Replacing mim install mmcv with raw pip --no-build-isolation removes mim's torch/CUDA wheel-matching and forces a source build. Fine in CI where torch is pinned, but a future cleanup back to mim would silently reintroduce the bug. Add a comment recording why pip is now required.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a pragmatic CI unblock that works but is under-audited. The dominant concern, flagged by all six reviewers, is that the setuptools<82 cap leaks from CI shell scripts into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires, propagating a transient build workaround to every downstream user. Secondary consensus issues are duplication of the pin across three sites with no shared revert criterion, an unexplained mmdet 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 bump riding along, and an undocumented --no-build-isolation that silently couples mmcv's build to ambient env state. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — accept the CI fix but pull the runtime pin out of setup.py and document the revert conditions.
